REVIEW FINDING (real, latent, same stale-list class the 05:56 #9 run fixed for the feedback inbox but left unpatched here): handleAnalytics aggregated with three flat kv.list({prefix, limit:1000}) calls then filtered to the last 30 days - KV lists lexicographically (oldest first), so once a prefix passed 1000 keys the NEWEST days would be silently dropped from the private /stats aggregates. Grounded via read-only KV API: pv: 121 keys now (~9/day -> cap hit organically ~Jan 2027), but flood vectors reach it in DAYS (400 registry-capped distinct pv: paths/day, ~1296 spoofable 2-char cc: codes/day). The old code could also exceed the 1000-subrequest/invocation ceiling under flood (3 lists + up to 3000 gets). FIX (loop-owned, minimal, 2 files): handleAnalytics now walks day-prefixes newest-first (mirroring readFeedback's fixed pattern; one limit-1000 page per day is complete since pv:<=400/ev:<=24/cc:<=1296 per day), with per-prefix key-read budgets (pv:400/ev:100/cc:300 -> worst case 90 lists + 800 gets = ~890 subrequests, inside the ceiling) and an honest `truncated:true` in the JSON when a budget trips; /stats renders an amber "read budget hit - newest days complete, oldest rows may be partial" note. The rest re-cleared: handlePing input validation + per-visitor (salted IP hash) caps on the 3 public scan-stats events + 400/day distinct-path registry + cc: regex normalization hold; log line carries only validated path/event (feedback free-text never logged); safeEqual constant-time gate holds (length-leak only, strong server secret); handleFeedback honeypot/category-allowlist/length-limits/200-day cap hold; handleScanStats 90 direct gets (no list scan, can't undercount itself) + honest 100k/pass floor hold. Unit-tested the new aggregation in node with a mock KV (1200 flood-minted pv: keys: newest 4 days complete, older dropped, truncated:true; ev/cc fully read under budget; 401 on wrong passphrase). CLEARED: Pro activation is fail-closed and sound - signature binds address + both tx hashes (verifyMessage over proActivationMessage), tx.from must equal the signer, burn leg proves DUMB ARRIVAL at dead (direct transfer() or allowlisted router swap with to=dead; arrival summed from receipt Transfer logs with computed keccak256 topic0, never hand-typed), model leg proves payment-token arrival at the server-configured model wallet (never client-supplied), each tx hash activates exactly once via never-expiring KV markers, chat sessions are short-lived (PRO_SESSION_MS) + signature-verified per request (claimed address alone unlocks nothing), free-tier caps are check-then-consume with the global budget consumed only after a SUCCESSFUL model call (provider hiccup can't burn quota), free models only so spend is $0 with OpenRouter's own 50/day cap as backstop. ChatMarkdown renders no HTML (React-escaped text, http/https links only) - no XSS from model output. ONE SHIP-WORTHY FINDING: the live-market system message in liveAnswerPro told Smiley "If a profile lists official websites/socials, share those when the user asks for links" - but DexScreener website/social fields are SELF-REPORTED by the token (anyone can list anything), so a malicious token could get its phishing "official" link served by Smiley carrying the hub's trust. FIXED (src/lib/ai/rag.ts, 1 line): links are now shared only as "self-reported by the token on DexScreener - anyone can list anything there, so never present them as hub-verified". NOTED-NOT-SHIPPED (minor, non-blocking): consumeCap is read-modify-write (no KV CAS) so concurrent bursts can overshoot caps by the in-flight count - OpenRouter's 50/day free cap is the real backstop, zero spend at stake; the grant-write/marker-write pair in handleAiProActivate isn't transactional - a KV partial failure between the two puts could let a retry re-activate on the same legs (needs a KV fault in a ms window; markers are otherwise write-once-tiny). NO SHIP-WORTHY FINDING - the claim flow holds up: (1) signed message binds name+address+timestamp; the username alphabet [a-zA-Z0-9_-] blocks message-format injection (no newlines possible) and the timestamp is bound to 10 min; (2) a captured signature can't be redirected - the address is inside the signed text and verifyMessage recovers against it, and cross-action replay fails (other verifiers check different messages); a within-window replay only re-sets the same name for the same wallet (benign no-op); (3) uniqueness via case-insensitive KV index; the check-then-set race is documented in the code (truly concurrent same-name claims, last-writer wins the index, self-heals on next set/clear - benign for a display-name registry); (4) XSS double-gated: alphabet enforced on POST AND re-validated on GET read-back, and leaderboards render names as React text ({displayName ?? shortAddr} - escaped); (5) clearing is also signature-verified; no wallet funds touch; POST rate-limited 10/day/IP (cf-connecting-ip hash); GET is public read-only with a 100-address validated/deduped cap. NOTED-NOT-SHIPPED: no reserved-name list - first-come-first-served by design, so "donatello"-class squats are possible; display names carry no official status, so reserving names is a product decision for Antonio, not a loop fix.

This run's #9 unit = adversarial review of the pledge surface (src/server/pledges.ts + src/lib/pledges.ts + src/components/dumb/PledgeCard.tsx + the epoch-scan redemption path in src/lib/burns.ts), not focused-reviewed since the feature shipped 2026-09-30. REVIEW FINDING (real, honesty-critical): redemption was computed from the wallet's ALL-TIME voluntary burns since the Sept-21 epoch block, with no time gate — a wallet with historical burns could pledge and get an instant "burned ✓" badge on a forward-looking promise ("I pledge to burn X within 30 days") without burning anything new, then re-pledge every 30 days for perpetual ✓ status on reputation they didn't re-earn. All numbers real (never invented), but the ✓ misattributed pre-promise burns to promise-keeping. FIX (loop-owned, minimal, 4 files): (1) POST /api/pledge now records the chain head block at pledge time (server-side eth_blockNumber on the existing rpc.pulsechain.com dependency — no new data source; fail-soft to null after signature verification so invalid requests never cost an RPC call and an RPC hiccup degrades to the pre-fix behavior); (2) EpochBurnRow gains per-tx `legs` (blockNumber/token/wei — additive, leaderboard/canvas untouched); (3) new pledgeBurnWei() counts only legs landing AFTER the pledge block, null-block legacy rows fall back to the all-time aggregate (honest, documented); (4) PledgeCard uses it for both the board badge and the share-redeemed flag, copy now states "burned since pledge" / "burns from before the pledge don't count". Pre-ship gate: tsc exit 0, eslint clean (prettier --fix on the copy lines), secrets grep clean, fresh-eyes diff review clean (exactly the intended change), npm run build + patch-wrangler clean, deployed to dump-money-hub-preview via the approved script ("Uploaded dump-money-hub-preview" line verified, version 7f88db97). Rest re-cleared: signed-message binding (name+address+timestamp) holds, 10-min sig window, per-IP 10/day rate limits on both write paths, amount allowlist (1000..10B whole tokens) holds, pledge TTL/expiry pruning holds, name index uniqueness race remains check-then-set (documented, self-healing — same class as username.ts, not ship-worthy), GET has no pagination but index is bounded to one entry per wallet and volume is ~0.

REVIEW FINDING (real, owner-safety not crash): readFeedback did a single kv.list({prefix:"fb:", limit:100}) - KV lists lexicographically (oldest first) with no reverse option, so once total feedback entries passed 100 the /stats inbox would silently go STALE, showing the 30 newest of the OLDEST 100 and hiding all new submissions from Antonio. Feedback volume is ~0 today so nothing was lost, but the failure mode is Antonio missing real bug reports. FIX (loop-owned, minimal, server-only): readFeedback now walks day-prefixes newest-first (fb:YYYY-MM-DD:, limit 1000 per day - always complete since the global cap is 200/day, 90-day window, early-exit at 30 items); same parse/truncate/sort logic, ts now taken from the walked day (identical value). Rest re-cleared: honeypot pretends 204 success without writing; category fixed allowlist; message 4..2000 chars; page pinned to "/"-leading <=200 chars else "/"; body cap 4096 bytes; global 200/day cap (noted: read-modify-write is non-atomic under burst, overshoot bounded by body size - accepted as a coarse brake, no clean atomic primitive in KV); /stats renders message as a React child (escaped, no XSS); keys unguessable enough (private read path only, behind the analytics passphrase). This run's #9 unit = adversarial review of the voluntary-burn flow (src/components/dumb/BurnBox.tsx - direct wallet burn + PLS-fallback swap burn), the money-adjacent surface where users burn their own tokens, not reviewed since the rally-link build. REVIEW FINDING (real, small): the "Burn with PLS" button's disabled condition (plsDisabled) omitted the direct path's isPending/isConfirming - asymmetric with canBurn, which DOES gate the direct button on !swapPending && !swapConfirming && !swapBusy. The hole: a direct burn awaiting its receipt drops the wallet balance on refetch, which can flip insufficient true and reveal the PLS panel MID-CONFIRMATION with the button armed - the user could fire a second burn path while the first is in flight, contradicting the stuck-note's own "do not start a second burn" advice. Both burns are honest (user-signed, to dead), so severity is low - but the double-spend-shaped interleaving was real. FIX (loop-owned, minimal, +10/-0): isPending || isConfirming added to plsDisabled, plus the same one-line early-return guard in startPlsBurn (belt-and-suspenders, matching doBurn's chain-guard style). Rest re-cleared: receipt-status gating (celebration, analytics, share all require status success - a reverted tx can never be celebrated); PLS fallback math honest (preTaxForArrival rounds up on the 87.4% floor, 8% slippage + 20-min deadline match the swap box - the copy is accurate); rally deep links strict-allowlisted (token DUMB|DAMP only, amount regex, prefill is intent-only - nothing burns without the wallet's own acknowledgment + signature; rally_open/rally_burn/burn_started are all in the analytics allowlist, so the funnel comments hold); the burned snapshot cannot celebrate pre-confirmation (share panel gated on doneHash + doneSucceeded); cross-path stale-state clears hold (resetSwap() in doBurn, reset() on swap success); both paths pin chainId 369; wallet error text rendered as React-escaped text (no injection sink); burn_voluntary fires once per confirmed hash via the trackedBurnFor ref. - 2026-10-02 08:53 ET run: backlog #9 DONE (security/safety hardening, recurring)
  -> audit-only, NO code changes, no build/deploy - the single src ship since
  the 08:13 #9 run (08:33 #13: failed-tx diagnosis in src/lib/tx-explain.ts)
  adversarially reviewed CLEAN, nothing found that earned a change. Reviewed:
  (1) Privilege: txClient is a read-only createPublicClient on PulseChain -
  the replay is a plain eth_call at block N-1, zero state change, no wallet,
  no signing, no new data source (the public RPC the scanner already used).
  (2) Evidence rules are receipt/block-anchored: out-of-gas (gasUsed >=
  gasLimit with a 0-limit guard), deadline (last arg of the three router
  methods decoded vs the inclusion block's timestamp via the retrying
  tryRead - a flake skips the check, never fakes it), replay-with-reason
  (3 attempts + backoff, reason-less errors retry, then degrade to null),
  gas cost from receipt math (null guards -> cost note omitted). (3)
  Fail-closed: every RPC flake lands on "unknown"/null and the honest
  "couldn't pin it down" fallback with the usual suspects - never "safe to
  retry", never a guess. (4) Revert-reason parsing: ABI Error(string) decode
  + template parse with the looksHumanReason gate (the pre-ship fix that
  caught viem's "with reason: 01." template junk, regression-tested on the

- 2026-10-02 06:53 ET run: backlog #9 DONE (security/safety hardening, recurring)
  -> audit-only, NO code changes, no build/deploy - the 06:33 #13 ship
  (contract-age line) adversarially reviewed CLEAN, nothing found that earned
  a change. Reviewed surface: findDeployBlock() + relAge() + the
  checkUpgradeability()->{check,isProxy} refactor + 3 age-check pushes in
  quickScan (src/lib/token-scan.ts), static copy in knowledge.ts/dump.ts.
  (1) Refactor blast radius: checkUpgradeability has ONE call site (quickScan
  line 2351) - the new tuple signature is consumed everywhere; no stale
  caller, tsc confirms.
  (2) Binary-search termination: standard first-true pattern (mid<hi whenever
  lo<hi, so both branches make progress) - terminates; each probe goes
  through tryRead (3 attempts + backoff, null on failure) so any RPC flake
  degrades the whole age line to "unknown", never a wrong number. Post-Cancun
  selfdestruct semantics make same-address redeploy effectively impossible,
  so first-code-block == deploy block; even so, the age line is an
  informational "pass", never a flag, with the hedge in the copy itself.
  (3) Banner/verdict semantics: the banner counts fail/warn/unknown only - a
  "pass" age check adds nothing; an "unknown" age check joins the unknowns
  count which the banner surfaces honestly ("No red flags found - N checks
  unknown"). Share copy uses fail/warn counts only - unaffected. "age" check
  id is unique (3 pushes of the same new check, no collision).
  (4) Fail-closed RPC paths: deployBlock null -> "unknown"; getBlock without
  timestamp -> "unknown"; proxy-check unknown returns isProxy=false but the
  age probes would almost surely have failed alongside (same RPC), so no
  reachable inconsistent-caveat state.
  (5) Privilege: read-only probes only (eth_getCode/getBlockNumber/getBlock)
  - no wallet, no signing, no new data source (the public RPC the scanner
  already used).
  (6) AI-knowledge copy verified against shipped code - matches the binary-
  search mechanism, the proxy-age caveat, and the context-not-verdict hedge.
  WATCHED, not shipped: ~25 sequential RPC reads add ~7s to every quick scan
  (06:33 measured on DUMB); worst-case flaky-RPC tryRead retries stretch it
  further before degrading to "unknown", and "Scan my bags" multiplies it per
  token. Latency only, never a safety lie - a parallelization pass is a future
  perf option, not a safety fix (minimalism: no churn on working safe code).

  and no admin path anywhere. NOTED, NOT CHURN (1): the name-uniqueness
  check-then-set can race (KV has no transactions) — two wallets claiming the
  same name in the same sub-second could both pass the check; both addr
  records would display the name while the index points at the last writer,

  defects on the brand-new public endpoint, both fixed. (1) Silent
  truncation undercount: the handler did `kv.list({prefix:"ev:", limit:1000})`
  and summed only what the list returned; the ev: namespace grows ~12
  events/day over the 90-day TTL (approaching 1000 keys), and once past the
  cap the lexicographically-first-1000 cutoff would silently drop the newest
  days — a public honesty surface undercounting its own numbers. (2) KV read
  amplification: that same list + one get per returned key meant up to ~1000
  KV GETs per uncached request on an unauthenticated GET — a cheap
  cache-busting DoS multiplier. The rewrite does 90 direct
  `kv.get("ev:<YYYY-MM-DD>:<event>")` reads (3 events × 30 days, key shape
  verified against the handlePing writer — same `dayKey`), three parallel
  event streams with sequential day reads; read count is bounded and the
  newest day can never fall out of a list cap. Response shape and numbers
  unchanged (verified: both domains return the same 3 deep scans / 1 pass /
  ≥100,000 DUMB floor the 03:50 run recorded — behavior-preserving).

Canonical tax framing (locked 2026-09-27, Antonio's words — use this everywhere,
never the old leg-first wording):
- DUMB: 6% on buy, sell, transfer — 5% instant burn, 1% reflections.
- DAMP: 3% on buy, sell, transfer — 2% instant burn, 1% reflections.
- "Instant": every leg executes atomically inside the transfer tx. The burn side =
  1% protocol burn to the dead address + bucket legs entombed forever (engine dead,
  owner renounced). Re-verified on-chain 2026-09-27 (fees 600/300, distributions
  (3333,3333,1667,1667)/(3333,0,3333,3334)).

Fee mechanics (verified 2026-09-26 — do not relitigate):
- DUMB 6% total tax: 2% contract buy-back bucket, 2% liquidity bucket, 1% burn,
  1% reflection. DAMP 3%: 1% contract, 1% burn, 1% reflection.
- The auto-processing engine is dead; the transfer tax, 1% burn, and ~1%
  reflection remain live. Never claim nothing burns on trades.

    RESIDUALS UPDATE (2026-09-30, 05:33 run): (a) the browser-supplied-address
    hole is CLOSED — paid chat + scan explainer now authorize on a SIGNED
    SHORT-LIVED PRO SESSION per request (the planned design), so the
    real-money-test precondition on THIS half is met; (b) KV replay guard
    remains non-atomic (get-then-put) but was ANALYZED benign: tx.from pins
    the grantee address (signature + from-match enforce it), so two
    concurrent writers with the same tx hashes must claim the same address
    and both writes land on the same `aipro:<addr>` / `aiprotx:<hash>` keys
    with ~identical values — no double-spend to a different wallet is
    possible. A Durable-Object transaction would be needed for a true
    atomic check; not worth the machinery for a same-key overwrite, so no
    code change on this half. The wallet signs
    `proSessionMessage(address, expiresAt)` (30-min TTL, expiry inside the
    signed bytes) once per half hour; the server verifies the signature
    (viem, local, no RPC) before any paid-model call or scan explainer, and
    quota accounting keys off the verified address. A claimed address alone
    now gets the free tier; the scan-explainer denial carries
    `sessionRequired: true` so the client re-signs and retries. Verified:
    crypto unit test (valid signs OK; tampered expiry / wrong address /
    expired / far-future / garbage all rejected), live POST on the custom
    domain (unproven address → proRequired + sessionRequired; free-tier
    question → live free answer, unaffected), served pro chunk carries the
    session message. Files: src/lib/ai/pro.ts (message + PRO_SESSION_MS),
    src/server/ai-pro.ts (verifyProSession), src/server/ai-chat.ts
    (enforcement), src/components/dumb/AiPreview.tsx (client sign + retry).
    No new data sources, no secrets in code, no wallet/signing beyond the
    user's own signMessage, zero mascot touch.

    2026-10-01 16:43 run) — `scripts/money-math.test.ts` (5 tests, `npm run
    test:money-math`, node:test, zero new dependencies) + tiny ESM alias
    loader (`scripts/test-alias-loader.mjs`, registered via
    `scripts/test-alias-hook.mjs`) so the tests import the REAL modules
    (not copies). Pins the one invariant that matters:
    `plsBurnMinOut({dumbOut: preTaxForArrival(T)}) >= T` for all probed T —
    dense sweep 0..200,000 raw units, 5k deterministic pseudo-random spread
    to 10^24, edges 0/1/10^24/pass threshold ±1 — plus the derived
    `PLS_BURN_TARGET_DUMB` clearing the 100k threshold at full slippage,
    a regression guard proving a round 110k buffer would NOT clear it
    (110k × 0.874 = 96,140 — the exact shipped bug), and MAX_MISSION_XP ==
    the max real daily award (tight, all types × daily). Negative control:
    a non-rounding preTaxForArrival variant fails the invariant at T=1,
    so the harness catches the bug class. tsc exit 0, eslint 0 errors,
    prettier clean. NO src changes → bundle byte-identical → no deploy.

  recipient is dead + amount > 0 + receipt Transfer log (from=tx.from, to=dead)
  — anything else 404s; the rendered amount comes from the successful calldata,
  which is exactly what the contract moved. (3) No cache poisoning: the
  1-year immutable cache applies only to the deterministic output (every input
  derives from the validated tx / on-chain bigint / deterministic seeds); 400s
  and 404s carry no cache header, so transient RPC flakes can't pin a false
  negative. (4) All rendered text is server-formatted or validated (unknown
  glyphs skipped); output is a PNG — no script path. (5) brag.tsx builds
  og:image only for TX_RE-valid txs (falls back to og-card.png),
  encodeURIComponent on og:url/canonical, explorerTx only ever sees validated
  hashes. (6) DoS amplification bounded: the expensive render only runs after
  full on-chain verification; per-isolate bg/flame/glyph caches. (7) The old
  POST-upload path is fully gone (no Cache/FormData remnants); the rename left
  no dangling imports. Also re-verified the 05:41 receipt-status gating still
  holds in BurnBox (share blocks render only under txSucceeded && hash).
